purpose: Plan animal and creature-adjacent game assets as source records before any sculpt, rig, Blender execution, or generated mesh. Each record maps visible anatomy, body plan, locomotion read, geometry terms, Blender tools, drawing tags, operator checks, and player-facing lore hooks.

transport, carrying, stable life, roads, courtyards, and trade routes
silhouette_rules: high readable shoulder and neck mass

animal_role_tiers.game_read: farm economy, kitchens, wool, hide, horn, bone, and village background life
material_rules: hide, fleece, bristle, horn, or hoof material slots

animal_role_tiers.game_read: farmyard motion, market cages, kitchen source, and low-cost flock dressing
silhouette_rules: beak and tail wedge visible from game camera

animal_role_tiers.game_read: cellars, alleys, ruin corners, plague mood, and scale reference
forest approach, hunting grounds, noble parks, and food chain signposting
silhouette_rules: ears or antlers readable above vegetation

animal_role_tiers.game_read: danger, wilderness pressure, heraldry, and night encounter staging
vault ceilings, caves, crypts, rafters, and ambient motion clusters
material_rules: thin membrane or small fur slots

source_support.label: Britannica - dog
source_support.support_summary: Supports dog as domestic canid reference with breed/body variation useful for settlement asset planning.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Small quadruped gait with alternating leg rhythm; first asset can be a static standing pose with future walk-cycle sockets.
operator_checks: Dog reads at top-down camera distance.
Four legs do not merge into one dark block.
Tail curve stays inside collision bounds unless intentionally raised.

lore_book_hooks.book_title: Kennel Marks Of The Lower Ward
lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Teaches the player to notice different warning and companion dog silhouettes around villages.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Describe why ear shape, tail carriage, and paw spacing matter more than fine fur on low-distance dogs.

source_support.label: Britannica - cat
source_support.support_summary: Supports cat as small domestic feline reference for compact quadruped and predator-adjacent proportions.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Low, flexible quadruped motion; first asset can support standing, sitting, and curled static variants from the same body plan.
operator_checks: Cat reads smaller than dog and rat remains clearly smaller than cat.
Ears stay visible from camera angle.
Curled pose still has a head/tail read.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Explains why farms with stored grain tend to show cat props near sacks, rafters, and pantry doors.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Tie the cat's pose to place: curled near warmth, alert near grain, perched near windows.

source_support.label: Britannica - horse
source_support.support_summary: Supports equine reference for long neck, hoofed limbs, mane, tail, and riding/working animal planning.

craft_sequence: place four leg columns with hoof blocks
animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Large quadruped gait with hooves under shoulder and hip masses; first asset is a static standing mount proxy with optional tack sockets.
operator_checks: Horse reads taller and longer than cattle.
Legs align under body mass instead of splaying randomly.
Saddle socket does not cut through spine line.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Lets the player interpret tack, hoof spacing, and stable stalls as world-building clues.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain why the barrel, shoulder, neck, and hoof spacing are enough for a readable mount proxy.

source_support.label: Britannica - donkey
source_support.support_summary: Supports donkey reference for equine body planning with pack-animal proportions and long ear silhouette.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Sturdy quadruped pack gait; source plan emphasizes static load balance and cargo attachment more than speed.
operator_checks: Long ears distinguish the asset from a small horse.
Pack load stays centered over torso.
Legs remain visible below cargo bags.

lore_book_hooks.book_title: On Pack Beasts And Narrow Ways
lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Connects cargo size, path width, and stable props to route planning inside the world.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Use the pack socket and long ears as the player's quick read.

source_support.label: Britannica - cattle
source_support.support_summary: Supports cattle reference for heavy ruminant body, horns, hooves, and domestic livestock planning.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Slow heavy quadruped with broad support stance; first asset can be static with yoke and cart attachment sockets.
operator_checks: Cattle reads heavier than horse.
Horn pair and broad head are visible from the main camera.
Yoke socket sits in front of shoulder mass.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Explains village labor assets and why yokes, carts, and field boundaries belong near cattle props.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Point out the horn, shoulder, and yoke-socket relationship.

source_support.label: Britannica - sheep
source_support.support_summary: Supports sheep reference for fleece, hoofed livestock, and wool-source planning.

source_support.label: Britannica - goat
source_support.support_summary: Supports goat reference for horned small-ruminant proportions and browsing livestock variants.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Small hoofed quadruped with flock spacing; first asset supports static grazing, standing, and clustered background variants.
operator_checks: Fleece shell does not hide all four legs.
Goat variant has horn/beard cues; sheep variant has stronger fleece read.
Clustered flock instances do not become one merged blob.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Links living flock assets to textile, dye, and market systems already documented elsewhere.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain fleece shell, shearing state, and why leg visibility keeps the animal readable.

source_support.label: Britannica - pig
source_support.support_summary: Supports pig reference for domestic swine body planning with snout, bristle, hoof, and boar variant cues.

craft_sequence: add tusk sockets for boar variant
animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Low heavy quadruped with short steps; first asset should read as pen animal or charging boar by head height and tusk option.
operator_checks: Snout disk is visible from front and side.
Short legs still show under belly.
Boar variant keeps tusks clear of collision proxy.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Teaches the player how farm swine and wild boar versions share a body plan but change danger read.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Use snout disk, belly height, and tusk sockets as the readable knobs.

source_support.label: Britannica - chicken
source_support.support_summary: Supports chicken reference for domestic poultry planning with beak, comb, feathers, legs, and flock use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Small bipedal bird walk with head bob; first asset can be static or simple flock scatter with clear beak direction.
operator_checks: Chicken reads as bird from distance, not as round rock.
Comb and beak survive low-poly LOD.
Legs are not wider than body.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Explains how poultry props mark food supply, household scale, and safe farm spaces.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Describe the egg body, comb tabs, and beak direction as the three essential reads.

source_support.label: Britannica - rat
source_support.support_summary: Supports rat reference for small rodent body planning with pointed muzzle, tail, ears, and urban/cellar use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Very small quadruped scurry; first asset emphasizes silhouette and scale over detailed limbs.
operator_checks: Rat stays tiny but readable beside barrels or food.
Tail is not thicker than body.
Scatter count does not become visual noise on lower compute hardware.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Tells the player that crumbs, tooth marks, and tiny silhouettes can signal hidden stores or decay.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Use scale, tail curve, and pantry context to make the rat feel placed.

source_support.label: Britannica - bat
source_support.support_summary: Supports bat reference for flying mammal body planning with wings, membranes, and cave/roost use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Flying and roosting body plan; first asset should support hanging static and broad-wing silhouette variants.
operator_checks: Bat reads by wingspan, not body detail.
Membrane stays thin and low-cost.
Cluster density is limited for lower compute hardware.

lore_book_hooks.book_title: Reading The Roof Of A Cave
lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Shows the player that ceiling silhouettes can reveal caves, hollows, and unused passages.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain wing membranes, roost sockets, and why clusters are budgeted separately.

source_support.label: Britannica - deer
source_support.support_summary: Supports deer reference for hoofed game body planning with antlers, thin legs, and alert forest silhouette.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Light hoofed quadruped; first asset prioritizes alert pose and antler/ear silhouette over detailed muscle.
operator_checks: Deer reads lighter than cattle and taller than dog.
Antler variant does not exceed intended bounds.
Thin legs remain visible against grass or forest floor.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Teaches tracking flavor: antlers, hoof prints, and alert posture imply nearby forests or noble hunting grounds.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Use the alert neck and antler span as the player's readable clues.

source_support.label: Britannica - gray wolf
source_support.support_summary: Supports wolf reference for wild canid body planning, predator posture, and heraldic/omen use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Canid predator gait with forward posture; first asset supports standing, stalking, and emblem/profile variants.
operator_checks: Wolf reads more threatening than village dog.
Fur ruff does not become random spikes.
Predator posture remains clear from side silhouette.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Uses wolf silhouettes, banners, and tracks as danger and faction flavor.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain how muzzle, ruff, and tail angle separate wolf from dog.

source_support.label: Britannica - crow
source_support.support_summary: Supports corvid reference for dark bird silhouettes, beak body planning, perched poses, and omen-style use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Perching and flying bird plan; first asset is a perched static bird with optional spread-wing emblem variant.
operator_checks: Beak direction is readable on dark material.
Perch claws align with rail, branch, roof, or grave marker.
Emblem variant stays symmetrical when requested.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Teaches the player to read perched dark birds as grave, tower, or omen flavor.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Describe beak wedge, tail fan, and perch socket as the core construction.

source_support.label: Britannica - fish
source_support.support_summary: Supports fish reference for streamlined aquatic body planning, fins, tail, scales, and food/river props.

craft_sequence: add scale bands or bump map
animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Aquatic swimming body plan; first asset supports static water/market props, with future swim path using body curve and tail direction.
operator_checks: Fish reads by lens body and tail fork even without scale detail.
Market variant can lie flat on platter.
Wet material works without decals on lower compute hardware.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Connects river ecology, market props, and kitchen clues.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain fins, tail fork, and scale bands as modeling choices that survive low detail.

source_support.label: Britannica - snake
source_support.support_summary: Supports snake reference for limbless reptile body planning, continuous curves, head shape, and symbolic use.

animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Limbless curve-driven body; first asset uses a drawn path with bevel thickness and pose selection instead of limb rigging.
operator_checks: Snake path does not self-intersect unless intentionally coiled.
Head wedge clearly shows direction.
Belly strip stays on underside or facing camera depending on pose.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Lets the player read snake tracks, staff carvings, and ritual symbols as the same curve grammar.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain path, bevel radius, head wedge, and belly strip as the four knobs.

source_support.label: Britannica - frog
source_support.support_summary: Supports frog reference for amphibian body planning with squat body, long hind legs, eyes, and wetland use.

craft_sequence: add front legs and webbed feet
animal_items.locomotion_mechanics: Squat jump body plan; first asset supports static crouch and low-cost hop-ready pose.
operator_checks: Eyes remain the dominant read at small size.
Rear legs signal jump without overcomplicating the mesh.
Wet material does not require decals.

lore_book_hooks.player_reward: Uses frogs near water, damp stone, and herbalist huts to make environments feel placed.
lore_book_hooks.detail_prompt: Explain squat body, eyes, and rear-leg arcs as the core readable details.
